arxiv-1810-13438.title: Particle dynamics simulation of wet granulation in a rotating drum Journal: Powder Technology
arxiv-1810-13438.creator: Thanh Trung Vo, Saeid Nezamabadi, Patrick Mutabaruka, Jean-Yves Delenne, Edouard Izard, Roland Pellenq, Farhang Radjai
arxiv-1810-13438.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Thanh Trung Vo, Saeid Nezamabadi, Patrick Mutabaruka, Jean-Yves Delenne, Edouard Izard, Roland Pellenq, Farhang Radjai. We simulate the granulation process of solid spherical particles in the presence of a viscous liquid in a horizontal rotating drum by using molecular dynamics simulations in three dimensions. The numerical approach accounts for the cohesive and viscous effects of the binding liquid, which is assumed to be transported by wet particles and re-distributed homogeneously between wet particles in contact.

arxiv-2104-13275.title: Exceptional field dependence of antiferromagnetic magnons in LiFePO 4
arxiv-2104-13275.creator: J. Werner, C. Neef, C. Koo, A. Ponomaryov, S. Zvyagin, R. Klingeler
arxiv-2104-13275.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Werner, C. Neef, C. Koo, A. Ponomaryov, S. Zvyagin, R. Klingeler. Low-energy magnon excitations in magnetoelectric LiFePO 4 have been investigated by high-frequency high-field electron spin resonance spectroscopy in magnetic fields up to B = 58 B=58 T and frequencies up to f = 745 f=745 GHz. For magnetic fields applied along the easy magnetic axis, the excitation gap softens and vanishes at the spin-flop field of B SF = 32 B_{\mathrm{SF}}=32 T before hardening again at higher fields.

arxiv-2211-02225.title: Automated Vehicle Highway Merging: Motion Planning via Adaptive Interactive Mixed-Integer MPC
arxiv-2211-02225.creator: Viranjan Bhattacharyya, Ardalan Vahidi
arxiv-2211-02225.description: Abstract A new motion planning framework for automated highway merging is presented in this paper. To plan the merge and predict the motion of the neighboring vehicle, the ego automated vehicle solves a joint optimization of both vehicle costs over a receding horizon.

arxiv-2502-09151.title: Regularization can make diffusion models more efficient
arxiv-2502-09151.creator: Mahsa Taheri, Johannes Lederer
arxiv-2502-09151.description: Abstract Diffusion models are one of the key architectures of generative AI. Their main drawback, however, is the computational costs. This study indicates that the concept of sparsity, well known especially in statistics, can provide a pathway to more efficient diffusion pipelines.

arxiv-2502-12050.title: SpeechT: Findings of the First Mentorship in Speech Translation
arxiv-2502-12050.creator: Yasmin Moslem Juan Julián Cea Morán* Mariano Gonzalez-Gomez* Muhammad Hazim Al Farouq*Farah Abdou* Satarupa Deb*
arxiv-2502-12050.description: Abstract This work presents the details and findings of the first mentorship in speech translation (SpeechT), which took place in December 2024 and January 2025. To fulfil the requirements of the mentorship, the participants engaged in key activities, including data preparation, modelling, and advanced research. \scalebox{0.5}{\faIcon[regular]{star}} \scalebox{0.5}{\faIcon[regular]{star}} footnotetext: Correspondence: yasmin[at]machinetranslation.

arxiv-2512-12048.title: Context-Aware Agentic Power Resources Optimisation in EV using Smart2Charge App *
arxiv-2512-12048.creator: Muddsair Sharif, Huseyin Seker
arxiv-2512-12048.description: Abstract This paper presents a nove context-sensitive multi-agent coordination for dynamic resource allocation (CAMAC-DRA) framework for optimizing smart electric vehicle (EV) charging ecosystems through the Smart2Charge application. The proposed system coordinates autonomous charging agents across networks of 250 EVs and 45 charging stations while adapting to dynamic environmental conditions through context-aware decision-making.

arxiv-2601-06165.title: What Users Leave Unsaid: Under-Specified Queries Limit Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2601-06165.creator: Dasol Choi, Guijin Son, Hanwool Lee, Minhyuk Kim, Hyunwoo Ko, Teabin Lim, Eungyeol Ahn, Jungwhan Kim, Seunghyeok Hong, Youngsook Song
arxiv-2601-06165.description: Abstract Current vision-language benchmarks predominantly feature well-structured questions with clear, explicit prompts. However, real user queries are often informal and underspecified. Users naturally leave much unsaid, relying on images to convey context. arxiv-2602-03811.title: Progressive Checkerboards for Autoregressive Multiscale Image Generation
arxiv-2602-03811.creator: David Eigen de@deigen.net
arxiv-2602-03811.description: Abstract A key challenge in autoregressive image generation is to efficiently sample independent locations in parallel, while still modeling mutual dependencies with serial conditioning. Some recent works have addressed this by conditioning between scales in a multiscale pyramid. Others have looked at parallelizing samples in a single image using regular partitions or randomized orders.

pmc-10660865.title: Chemical Intolerance and Mast Cell Activation: A Suspicious Synchronicity
pmc-10660865.creator: Raymond F. Palmer, Tania T. Dempsey, Lawrence B. Afrin
pmc-10660865.description: Background: Chemical Intolerance (CI) is characterized by intolerances for chemicals, foods, and drugs with multi-system symptoms. As yet, the biomechanism remains unclear. One study reported converging lines of evidence supporting a substantive association between mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) and CI.

pmc-11398899.title: MED12 and CDK8/19 Modulate Androgen Receptor Activity and Enzalutamide Response in Prostate Cancer
pmc-11398899.creator: Chiara Andolfi, Caterina Bartolini, Elisa Morales, Büşra Gündoğdu, Martin Puhr, Juan Guzman, Sven Wach, Helge Taubert, Achim Aigner, Iris E Eder, Florian Handle, Zoran Culig
pmc-11398899.description: Prostate cancer progression is driven by androgen receptor (AR) activity, which is a target for therapeutic approaches. Enzalutamide is an AR inhibitor that prolongs the survival of patients with advanced prostate cancer. However, resistance mechanisms arise and impair its efficacy. One of these mechanisms is the expression of AR-V7, a constitutively active AR splice variant.

pmc-12563931.title: Comparison of Conventional Root Tip Resection with Digitally Guided Resection—An In Vitro Study
pmc-12563931.creator: Paul Kübel, Aydin Gülses, Juliane Wagner, Cedric Hinrichs, Jörg Wiltfang, Johannes Spille
pmc-12563931.description: Background/Objectives: In oral and maxillofacial surgery, apicoectomy is a standard procedure for treating persistent periapical infections after insufficient conservative treatment. Traditional techniques rely on direct visualization, while navigated methods offer advantages in precision and safety. This in vitro study compared conventional apicoectomy with dynamically guided navigation.

pmc-12635375.title: snRNA-seq reveals key transcription factors in the inflammatory response of microglia after intracerebral hemorrhage
pmc-12635375.creator: Zhuojin Wu, Danyang Chen, Shiling Chen, Ge Zhang, Xuan Wu, Kai Shu, Chao Pan, Zhouping Tang
pmc-12635375.description: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severe neurological disease with limited treatment options. Microglia, the primary immune cells of the brain, contribute significantly to secondary injury following ICH, exhibiting heterogeneity in response across different stages of ICH. However, the exact mechanisms regulating this process remain incompletely elucidated.

pmc-13365246.title: Sharpness matters: Higher image resolution improves generalization and explainability in chest X-ray classification
pmc-13365246.creator: Aditya V. Kulkarni, John R. Zech, Paul H. Yi
pmc-13365246.description: Deep learning (DL) chest radiograph (CXR) models are often trained on downsampled images to reduce computational overhead, despite clinical workflows operating at high resolution. Previous studies have investigated the impact of input resolution on CXR classification accuracy, yet two fundamental pillars of safe and trustworthy AI, explainability and generalizability, remain underexplored.
